title: What the implementer did with the spec it was given
description: The round's account of its own work. A round that records none, and a round that records unfinished work, both stop the pull request for a person to read — so an honest `unfinished` costs nothing that silence does not cost too.

status.description: complete only when you finished everything this dispatch handed you and `unfinished` is empty; unfinished otherwise. It is about the work you were given — a spec, a findings record, or a failing check — and never about anything you were not given: a fixer handed findings or a failing check answers for those and says nothing about a spec it never had. Claiming complete for work you did not finish is worse than saying unfinished, because the run stops for a person either way and only one of the two tells them the truth.

summary.description: One or two sentences on what you changed, written for the person deciding whether this may merge.

unfinished.description: Every part of the work you were given and did not do, with the reason — including work you were told to do and could not: a file the spec names that does not exist, two statements that contradict, a repair that is a decision for a person. An empty array when nothing was left. A fixer reports here on the findings or the failing check it was handed, never on a spec it was not given.

part.description: Which part of the work this is, named the way the thing you were given names it.

reason.description: Why it was left undone, in a sentence a person can act on.
